# GlanceVNC

> GlanceVNC is a paid VNC and RDP remote-desktop app by Chris Russell for iPhone and iPad. It lets users view and control computers they own or are authorised to access.

## Product facts

- Version 1.2 requires iOS 18 or later on iPhone, or iPadOS 18 or later on iPad.
- Connects to Mac, Windows PC, Linux and Raspberry Pi computers running a compatible VNC or RDP server, or Mac Screen Sharing, that the iPhone or iPad can reach. GlanceVNC is a client, not a VNC server or hosted remote-access relay.
- Connect over the local network, or remotely through the user's own VPN that provides access to the computer.
- All features are included in the app purchase. No subscriptions, in-app purchases or GlanceVNC account are required. Regional prices are shown in the App Store.
- RDP supports compatible Windows and Linux desktops, direct TLS/NLA connections and username/password sign-in (port 3389 by default). Add RDP hosts manually; nearby discovery finds VNC services. RDP gateways, Kerberos/Azure sign-in, clipboard, audio and file/device redirection are not supported.
- Review RDP certificates in the app when approval is needed. Approval is remembered; changed certificates require a new review. Edit the connection to forget a trusted certificate.
- Version 1.2 adds iOS/iPadOS 18 and later support, adaptive system styling, improved landscape and larger-text layouts, and a desktop rendering compatibility fix. Check the App Store for release availability.
- Version 1.1 introduced RDP and improved VNC colour-format compatibility and RDP graphics setup, and added an explanation when no RDP desktop image arrives within 15 seconds.
- Hide the keyboard with its dismissal button or by tapping the desktop in Touch or Trackpad mode; the desktop tap still sends the usual remote click.
- Settings → What’s New lists recent improvements alongside third-party licences and the privacy policy.
- Features include saved connections, nearby Bonjour discovery, Touch and Trackpad controls, keyboard input, gesture help, colour-depth preferences and custom backgrounds.
- Switch Touch/Trackpad mode during a session through session Settings. Home-screen Settings controls the default for future connections.
- Compatible legacy Apple Remote Desktop authentication and standard VNC password authentication are supported. Newer Apple Screen Sharing authentication, Tight Security and VeNCrypt are not supported; see the support page for details.

## Privacy and storage

Saved connection metadata can sync through the user's private iCloud database, including protocol, approved RDP certificate fingerprint, remote computer profile and VNC sharing preference. Passwords are stored separately in Apple Keychain and can sync through iCloud Keychain when enabled. Desktop thumbnails and custom backgrounds stay on the device. The app does not send remote desktop content to the developer or include advertising, tracking SDKs or in-app analytics collection. The website separately uses Google Analytics to measure visits and page usage. See the privacy policy for full details.

## Setup guides

- [Guides](https://glancevnc.com/guides/): Step-by-step remote desktop setup walkthroughs.
- [Mac mini from iPad with VNC and Tailscale](https://glancevnc.com/guides/mac-mini-ipad-vnc-tailscale/): Configure Mac Screen Sharing with a VNC password, connect locally, then use the Mac’s Tailscale address. Tailscale is a separate network service requiring its own sign-in, not a built-in GlanceVNC integration.
